title: Scoped adjunct collab snapcount — coverage & effort (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, scoped spreadsheet-style snapshot to: 1) surface immediate coverage gaps across adjacent teams for a targeted surge window (Apr 24-30), 2) estimate ad-hoc effort to cover gaps, and 3) assign short-lived owners for handoff. This is intentionally lightweight - inputs are fuzzy, numbers are back-of-envelope and meant to seed follow-ups.

Context / why now:
- Multiple product rollouts next week with cross-region fallback tests.
- SRE + Support indicated ~30% higher pager volume for feature X in canary region.
- We need a compact owner list + rough hours estimate to staff temporary surge coverage so SLAs don't degrade.

Snapshot (per-region quick rows):
Region | Adjacent team | Current on-call overlap (hrs/day) | Expected delta (pages/day) | Quick effort estimate (hrs total, Apr24-30) | Suggested short owner
---
us-west | infra-provisioning | 4 | +18 | 14 | Liam Chen
us-east | serving-runtime | 6 | +10 | 10 | Sofia Martinez
eu-central | observability | 3 | +6 | 8 | Diego Alvarez
apac | platform-eng | 2 | +12 | 12 | Ava Patel

Notes on numbers: estimates are summed across 7 days. "Current on-call overlap" is hours per day where adjacent team already has duty that can triage. "Expected delta" is derived from recent canary traffic pattern multiplied by weekend uplift factor 1.2. "Quick effort estimate" assumes ~1.5 hours per extra page + coordination overhead.

Back-of-envelope econ (very rough):
- Weighted average engineer fully-loaded hourly = $90/hr (for costing only).
- Estimated temp staffing cost = (14+10+8+12) * $90 = 44 * 90 = $3,960.
- If we instead shift traffic to fallback model for the week (operator effort 10 hrs to configure + $900), fallback is materially cheaper but has product risk.

Proposed short plan (one-week cadence):
1) Confirm owners (by Apr 12 EOD) - owners below to ack.
2) Owners to post a 1-paragraph triage playbook in the shared Slack channel (template below).
3) Daily 09:30 stand (10m) Apr24-30 - quick roll-call + escalation hits.
4) If page rate > projected by 30% two days in a row, trigger fallback runbook (see linked_artifacts).

Suggested Slack playbook template (owners copy/paste):
- Scope: what alerts you own for Apr24-30 (alert IDs)
- First action: triage checklist (quick triage step list)
- Escalation path: who to loop at +30% trend
- Postmortem owner: (name)

Assigned owners (please ack in thread):
- Liam Chen - us-west infra-provisioning (est 14 hrs).
- Sofia Martinez - us-east serving-runtime (est 10 hrs).
- Diego Alvarez - eu-central observability (est 8 hrs).
- Ava Patel - apac platform-eng (est 12 hrs).

Open questions / loose edges:
- Do we have spare SRE capacity if multiple regions spike at once? (SRE lead to answer).
- Should customer-success be pre-notified for key enterprise tenants in these regions? (CS lead).
- Are there any scheduled infra maintenance windows that overlap Apr24-30 that would reduce effective coverage?

Immediate next steps (owner / due):
- Owners ack this doc in thread (All) / due: Apr 12 EOD.
- SRE lead (TBD) confirm cross-region reserve capacity / due Apr 14.
- Product PM (linked as CONFLUENCE-1223) confirm canary scaling assumptions / due Apr 15.

Scratch log (notes-to-self style):
- If fallback chosen, add 6 hrs for monitoring dashboard tweaks + 4 hrs for customer messaging.
- Consider lightweight synthetic probe ramp (0.5hr setup per region) to validate fallback routing quickly.
- Keep this doc small - move verified numbers into product/ops working sheet if we go beyond April window.

Bottom line: this is a pragmatic, minimal tracker to get temporary owners, a rough cost view, and a contingency route. Numbers are not final; goal is triage and an owner list for Apr24-30.

Version history:
- 2026-04-10: initial snapshot (Ava Patel)
- 2026-04-12: added eu-central adjust and econ calc, assigned owners (collabs)
